search_log: Searched “Funny Story Emily Henry official excerpt first chapter Penguin Random House”; found and opened Penguin’s sustained publisher excerpt and its sample-PDF listing.
Searched “Funny Story Emily Henry excerpt Daphne Miles chapter”; found and opened ELLE’s authorized Berkley-credited interior excerpt.

Searched “Funny Story Emily Henry point of view first person narrator Daphne” and “Funny Story Emily Henry review first-person narration”; opened explicit whole-book descriptions from The Romance Report and SuperSummary.

Searched “Funny Story single POV Emily Henry” plus Publishers Weekly and Library Journal domain queries; results corroborated single-Daphne POV, while Publishers Weekly’s opened/searchable review summarized plot but did not explicitly identify narrative person and was not used as person evidence.
Targeted searches for multiple narrators, alternating point of view, epistolary structure, diary, or frame narration produced no credible contrary structural evidence.
person_note: The quote corpus repeatedly exposes Daphne as a participating “I” narrator across recollection, present action, reflection, and speech beats. Generic “you” statements are maxims or dialogue, not sustained second-person narration; bare references to “he” or “she” do not establish third person. Publisher-authorized opening and interior excerpts independently sustain the same first-person voice, and whole-book sources explicitly identify Daphne as the first-person narrator. No evidence indicates alternating narrators or a frame structure; the only uncertainty concerns a few context-poor gnomic quotations, which does not affect the book-level classification.
